candidate.name: Josh Oppenheimer
candidate.credentials: MD (Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai), MBA (Cambridge Judge Business School), AB Public & International Affairs (Princeton), board-certified Emergency Medicine, practicing physician in DC/Maryland
candidate.background: Co-founded Transformative AI during residency; served as CMO and ultimately CEO through 2023. Built AI to predict/prevent Sudden Cardiac Arrest, raised $4M+ (Wellcome Trust, Innovate UK), led a team of 8, ran clinical research with hospitals in the US/UK/Estonia, engaged FDA on regulatory pathway (SaMD). Full founder journey: fundraising, team-building, co-founder departure, winding down the company. Now advises early-stage health AI founders on product strategy, GTM, sales, and regulatory pathways.
strengths_for_matching: General/Emergency Medicine clinical background (not surgical or mental-health-specific)
Product strategy and clinical workflow integration
Sales / BD / customer relationships in healthcare settings
Founder/CEO experience including fundraising, scaling, and winding down a company

functions_of_interest: Clinical/Medical Affairs roles that are NOT direct patient care (e.g. Medical Director of Product, Head of Clinical Strategy, VP Medical Affairs)
Product (VP Product, Chief Product Officer, Head of Product)
BD / Partnerships / Sales (VP Business Development, Head of Partnerships, VP Sales, Head of Customer Success)
must_not_require: Direct clinical supervision of practicing staff
Role primarily or solely focused on clinical research or clinical studies — clinical research can be one element of the job but should not be the dominant or defining responsibility
role_preferences.ideal_intersection: Clinical medicine + product + sales/customer relationships, applied to using AI to improve healthcare delivery or outcomes
role_preferences.title_flexibility: Does not need to be 'Chief Medical Officer' specifically. Open to VP/Director/Head-level titles, as long as a medical/clinical background (MD or equivalent) is a stated requirement or a clear differentiator for the role.
engagement_types: Fractional / part-time exec (e.g. Fractional CMO, Fractional Head of Clinical/Product)
role_preferences.engagement_note: Fractional and part-time executive roles are welcome alongside full-time roles. Apply the same functional/exclusion/domain criteria; for fractional roles, treat the min_base_salary_usd floor as a pro-rated/retainer-equivalent guide rather than a strict full-time-equivalent cutoff — use judgment and flag the compensation structure (e.g. day rate, monthly retainer, equity) in the digest. Note: niche fractional roles (e.g. geriatrics-focused home health CMO) are acceptable on a fractional basis even when the clinical domain is less central to Josh's background.

company_preferences.late_stage_note: Open to late-stage/public companies only if culture reads as dynamic and fast-moving, not bureaucratic. De-prioritize large, slow-moving incumbents.
exclude_employer_types: Health insurers / payers (e.g. Aetna, UnitedHealth, BCBS and subsidiaries)
Hospital systems / health systems as direct employer
Pure EHR / legacy health IT vendors (e.g. Epic, Cerner, Athenahealth)
company_preferences.clinical_domain_preference: Cast a wide net across digital health/health AI. Favor roles where a general medicine or emergency medicine background is a clear advantage (e.g. acute care, urgent care, primary care, care navigation/triage, remote monitoring, multi-specialty platforms). De-prioritize (but don't hard-exclude) companies narrowly focused on surgery or mental health, where the EM/general background is less of a differentiator. Score low: companies whose product is exclusively radiology/imaging (e.g. automated MRI/CT reading, radiology workflow tools) — these require a radiologist, not an EM physician, as the clinical differentiator. Consumer wellness / non-medical wearables (e.g. fitness trackers) score low — prefer companies whose product touches actual clinical care.
company_preferences.product_mission_preference: Strong preference for companies whose core product directly improves clinical care quality, patient outcomes, or clinical decision-making. De-prioritize companies whose primary value proposition is hospital business operations, revenue cycle management, billing optimization, or coding accuracy — even if they use AI and sell to health systems. Examples of preferred focus: diagnosis support, care navigation, treatment optimization, patient monitoring, clinical workflow tools used by clinicians at the point of care. Examples to score lower: CDI (clinical documentation improvement for billing), RCM automation, prior auth processing.
company_preferences.geography: Company HQ can be anywhere, but the product/role should be US-focused

logistics.location_preference: Remote, or hybrid in the DC/Maryland area (any in-office frequency is acceptable, not a filter)
logistics.travel_exception: Will consider roles requiring more than 25% travel ONLY if the base salary is explicitly listed at $400,000 or above. If salary is not listed and travel appears to exceed 25%, include the listing but flag the travel concern prominently.
logistics.salary_filter_note: If salary is not listed, do not auto-exclude — include if otherwise a strong match and flag salary as 'not listed'. Exclude only if a listed range falls entirely below the floor.

job_boards: General web search for relevant role titles + 'digital health' / 'health AI'
General web search for 'fractional CMO' / 'fractional medical director' / 'fractional clinical advisor' + 'digital health' / 'health AI'
funding_alert_sources: PR Newswire / BusinessWire health AI funding press releases
Crunchbase / PitchBook recent health AI raises
General web search: 'health AI' OR 'digital health' funding raised million 2026

logic.seed_or_series_a: Flag if the company has NO physician (MD/DO) on the founding team or listed leadership. Josh would reach out to a board member, investor, or team member to explore whether they are considering a CMO hire enabled by the new capital. Priority: HIGH.
logic.series_b_or_later: Flag even if they already have an MD on the team — they are likely expanding the team and may be creating new clinical leadership roles. Josh would reach out to explore upcoming hiring plans. Priority: MEDIUM.
logic.any_stage_no_md: If a company at any stage raised $10M+ and has no MD on leadership, flag as HIGH priority outreach regardless of round.

funding_alerts.outreach_target: Identify the best outreach contact for each flagged company: founding CEO (if accessible), lead investor (partner at lead VC firm), or a known team member. Include their name and LinkedIn URL if findable.
funding_alerts.digest_section: Include as a separate 'Outreach Opportunities' section in the digest, after job listings. Each entry: company name, amount raised, round, lead investor(s), clinical AI product description, whether they have an MD on team, outreach target, and 1-sentence rationale for why Josh's background is relevant.

scoring_notes.SmarterDx: Excluded — product is primarily CDI/revenue cycle (billing optimization), not direct clinical care improvement.
scoring_notes.Hippocratic AI: Deprioritize roles with >25% travel unless base salary is explicitly $400k+. MD/DO-required customer success roles are relevant but flag travel requirement.
scoring_notes.Whoop: Score low (4/10) — consumer wearable/fitness tracker, not clinical care AI. Salary also likely below floor.
scoring_notes.Navina: Keep an eye on — Series C primary care AI, worth checking if Senior Medical Manager requires MD. Direct company URL format may not work; find apply link via LinkedIn or Greenhouse instead.
scoring_notes.Bayesian Health: Fractional roles OK but flag if the primary responsibility is clinical studies/regulatory submissions rather than product/commercial work.
scoring_notes.Jukebox Health: Fractional/niche roles acceptable even though geriatrics focus is not Josh's primary domain.
scoring_notes.Vista AI: Score low — radiology/imaging automation (MRI acquisition). Clinical domain is radiology-specific; a radiologist, not an EM physician, is the natural differentiator. Not a good fit.
scoring_notes.Nitra: Score low — AI-native practice management OS (finance, procurement, back-office operations for outpatient clinics). Product is primarily operational, not clinical care improvement. Josh also has no outpatient clinic operations background to offer.
scoring_notes.Assort Health: MEDIUM-HIGH for funding outreach. Patient access/scheduling AI (voice agents for healthcare call centers). Less directly clinical than ideal but large company with no MD on exec team. Surface again if they post a role with clinical product or clinical strategy responsibilities.
scoring_notes.Cadence: HIGH for funding outreach — chronic disease RPM (hypertension, diabetes, heart failure, COPD) with no CMO/MD on exec team. Very strong clinical domain fit for EM physician. Surface job postings if they appear.
scoring_notes.Prenosis: HIGH for funding outreach — FDA-cleared AI sepsis diagnostics (Sepsis ImmunoScore). Best clinical domain match in the funding digest (acute care, sepsis = core EM). CEO is Bobby Reddy Jr., PhD engineer. Series A. Surface any job postings.
scoring_notes.OpenEvidence: HIGH for funding outreach — AI clinical decision support used by 40%+ of US physicians. No MD on founding team. Series D / $12B valuation — may have grown clinical staff not in public profiles; worth checking before outreach. Surface any job postings.
scoring_notes.Doctronic: MEDIUM for funding outreach — AI autonomous prescribing/consultations (Series B). Already has CMO Dr. Byron Crowe, but expanding rapidly. Surface clinical product or VP-level roles.
scoring_notes.Qualified Health: MEDIUM for funding outreach — enterprise AI governance platform for health systems (Series B). CMO is Dr. Kedar Mate (strong). May be hiring for commercial/BD leadership. Surface relevant postings.
scoring_notes.xCures: Surface for funding outreach — medical records AI (Series B, June 2026). Less directly clinical (data structuring infrastructure) but no MD on team. Lower clinical relevance than Cadence/Prenosis.

watchlist.note: Add company names to include_companies (always surface regardless of other criteria) or exclude_companies (never surface). scoring_notes is informal guidance on companies seen before.
